title: Marshall-Lerner and J-Curve
welcome_lead: When does devaluation actually fix a trade deficit?
meta_desc: A-Level Exchange Rates: Marshall-Lerner condition and J-curve.
final_note: Devaluation only improves trade if combined elasticities exceed one.

concepts.def: Trade balance improves after devaluation only if PED of exports + PED of imports is greater than 1.
Trade balance worsens before improving after devaluation.
How quickly exchange rate changes feed into prices.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Marshall-Lerner condition: PED of exports + PED of imports must exceed 1 for a devaluation to improve the trade balance.

Short run, contracts and habits mean quantities respond slowly. The trade balance gets worse first as imports cost more in domestic currency. Then quantities adjust and the balance improves - the J shape.
Politicians who devalue hoping for instant improvement are often disappointed. The full effect takes 18 to 24 months. Pass-through and price-setting habits delay the recovery.
